judgment.rationale: Both endpoints sit at BASIC 3 (rank 2), so direction rests on substantive content, not rank. The second SFI (B3.2.2.1.1, Reading / Phonics) asks learners to 'Understand the relationship between spelling of words and sounds of speech', under the parent Content Standard 'Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write' — an explicit link from phonic sound-letter knowledge to writing. The first SFI (B3.4.9.3.2, Writing / Writing as a Process) requires learners to 'Proofread draft to correct punctuation and spelling errors', with a supplied Learning Component 'Proofread draft to correct spelling errors'. Grasping grapheme–phoneme/spelling–sound correspondences plausibly supports the likelihood of success in detecting and correcting misspellings while proofreading one's own draft, so the phonics indicator builds towards the proofreading indicator. The shared evidence is not mere repeated wording: the token overlap ('spelling') is backed by a substantive skill link from decoding/encoding knowledge to applied spelling correction. Note the first indicator also covers punctuation, which the phonics indicator does not support, limiting the scope of the dependency; confidence is moderate accordingly. Source-evidence truncation on both endpoints and LC truncation on the second SFI mean some supporting exemplar text is unavailable.
